summary: Tested Broadcast-Bewertungssystem (Broadcast Rating Feature). Found and fixed critical backend bug: broadcasts were created with UUID user_id but conversations API used ObjectId string as user_id, causing customer to never see broadcasts. Fixed 1 line in server.py. All 8 test scenarios now PASS.

critical.issue: FIXED: Broadcast created conversation participants using user.get('user_id') UUID, but GET /api/messages uses str(_id) ObjectId as user_id. Caused customers to never see broadcasts in their messages. Fixed to always use str(u['_id']).

critical_code_review_comments: The user ID inconsistency (UUID user_id vs ObjectId str) is a systemic risk. Audit all places using current_user.get('user_id') vs current_user.get('id') to ensure correct field is used.
updated_files: /app/backend/server.py (line ~2523: uid = str(u['_id']) if u.get('_id') else u.get('user_id'))
context_for_next_testing_agent: Broadcast feature fully working after fix. Admin can send broadcasts, customers see them in /messages as InkBook News conversation with dark card UI, rating buttons (star/x) work, thanks message shows after rating, no double voting, admin sees updated counts. Bug was: broadcast used UUID from user_id field but conversations API used ObjectId string.

rca_of_issue: RCA: In POST /api/admin/broadcast, line 2523: uid = u.get('user_id') or (str(u['_id']) ...). For users with a UUID 'user_id' field (created via Google auth then given JWT), this used UUID. But GET /api/messages uses current_user.get('id') = str(_id) ObjectId. Conversations queried by {participants: str(_id)} never matched conversations created with UUID participants. Fix: uid = str(u['_id']) if u.get('_id') else u.get('user_id')
